narrative:
# INITIAL INCIDENT REPORT

**To:** Plant Manager (Hazira); Asset HSE Lead; Statutory authorities under ERDMP notification requirements
**From:** Health & Safety Manager, Hazira Gas Processing Complex
**Date / time of report:** 24 September 2020, mid-day IST (filed within 6 hours of all-clear)
**Incident type:** Hydrocarbon vapour release with subsequent fire — Phase I, Gas Terminal area
**Status:** Plant in emergency shutdown; affected area cordoned and under guard; site investigation begun. **Cause and root cause not yet established.**

---

## 1. Summary of event

In the early hours of this morning a hydrocarbon vapour release occurred from the 36" condensate metering skid in the Gas Terminal area (Phase I). The release was first detected by perimeter security at approximately 02:15 hrs. The vapour cloud accumulated for approximately 56 minutes during which plant personnel attempted, but were physically unable, to approach and locate the source on foot due to gas density. At **03:08:15 hrs (timestamp from plant CCTV)** the cloud ignited and developed into a major fire affecting the metering skid and the immediately surrounding piping. The fire was contained by the on-site fire team and brought under control by approximately 06:00 hrs. The Plant Manager, acting as Commander-in-Charge, declared all-clear at **07:30 hrs** following confirmation of zero LEL and a complete personnel head-count.

**Casualties / injuries (as of this report):** Nil to plant personnel and on-shift contractors. CISF have confirmed no injuries inside the plant boundary. Status of the surrounding shanty/civilian area outside the plant perimeter is being verified with the district authorities and CISF; this report will be updated.

**Cause:** Under investigation. Working hypotheses are stated in §10 below; they are hypotheses only.

---

## 2. Plant and facility context

Hazira Gas Processing Complex receives gas and associated condensate from Mumbai Offshore production via two submarine pipelines: 36" (commissioned 1986, ~230 km) and 42" (commissioned 1996, ~244 km). Plant throughput capacity ~46.9 mmscmd. Major downstream consumers include the HVJ pipeline network, KRIBHCO fertiliser plant, and NTPC power generation.

The Gas Terminal area (Phase I) is the inlet receiving section where the offshore stream is separated and routed downstream. The condensate metering skid at issue contains two parallel 6" meters in service — **310FT01** and **310FE2** — measuring condensate flow downstream of the slug catcher. Both meters are part of the original 1986 plant inventory.

**Relevant recent maintenance activity in the affected area:**

- **17 September 2020:** SAP Notification 3800419840 raised by operations for malfunction of meter 310FT01.
- **18 September 2020:** Retaining-plate gasket of meter 310FT01 replaced. Per the maintenance team's verbal account this morning, the original OEM gasket specification (a 1986 rectangular-slot design) is not currently held on file at site, and the replacement was effected using a substitute O-ring procured locally. After installation, the system was pressurised to operating pressure with both meters in line and isolated; **no separate hydrostatic test to design pressure was performed.**
- **19 September 2020:** Meter 310FT01 returned to service, ~46 hours after the gasket replacement.
- This gasket replacement is the **third on this meter in the past 22 months** (previous replacements: November 2018, February 2019). Investigation should determine whether the recurrence pattern was treated as a reliability concern.

---

## 4. Personnel accounts (de-identified by role)

Statements were taken this morning between 09:00 and 11:30 hrs from the seven personnel directly involved in the detection-to-isolation phase. Original signed statements are held in the H&S office; summaries below.

- **CISF Constable A — Watch Tower 3 (NW periphery):** "Heard a sharp hissing noise around 02:15. Saw a vapour cloud rising behind the Gas Terminal area. Informed CISF Main Gate, Fire Station and LPG Control Room by intercom."
- **CISF Head Constable B — Gas Terminal Gate (East):** "Heard noise at the same time, saw vapour. Informed CCTV Control Room and CISF Main Gate."
- **CISF Sub-Inspector C — CCTV Control Room:** "Took the call from Head Constable B at 02:15. On the monitor I could see heavy leakage near the metering skid. I called the Gas Terminal Control Room at 02:18."
- **Chief Engineer (Production) — Gas Terminal CR:** "On night duty from 20:00 hrs. Around 02:20 the annunciator alarmed and the CCTV operator phoned. We saw a heavy cloud out of the window. The Junior Engineer and I went out together to try and reach the metering area. The cloud was so dense and the smell so strong that we could not get close. We came back and I phoned the GSP Shift In-charge, LPG Shift In-charge and the CFU Panel Engineer."
- **Junior Engineer (Mechanical) — Gas Terminal CR:** Confirms the Chief Engineer's account. Adds that visibility outside the control room was extremely poor.
- **DGM (Production) — GSP Shift In-charge:** "Got the call at about 02:35. Reached the Gas Terminal Gate with the Overall Shift In-charge. We couldn't enter — the smell was overpowering. I closed MOV 54 at 03:01."
- **GM (Production) — Overall Shift In-charge / SIC:** "Got the call at 02:35. Reached the Gas Terminal Gate. Instructed closure of the 36" PCV from the Gas Terminal CR. Informed Fire Station, Resident Engineer, Head Operations and the Plant Manager. By the time the senior team arrived the fire had started."

## 5. Initial site observations (post-extinguishment walk-down, 08:30–11:00 hrs)

The site was made safe by the fire team after 07:30. I conducted a controlled walk-down of the affected area beginning 08:30 hrs accompanied by the Resident Engineer and the Mechanical Maintenance lead. Photographs have been taken; an annotated photo set will follow this report. **All damaged equipment and the surrounding debris field has been cordoned and is under guard; nothing has been moved or disturbed pending forensic inspection.**

Visible findings at this stage (descriptive, not yet causal):

- **Meter 310FT01:** retaining plate extensively damaged; all bolts of the flange arrangement are out. The meter assembly appears to be the most severely damaged single item in the area.
- **Meter 310FE2 (the parallel 6" meter):** comparatively much less damaged — only one bolt of the flange arrangement is damaged.
- **Surrounding condensate piping:** multiple lines around the metering skid are buckled, ruptured or displaced. This is fire-induced damage; it does not, on visual inspection, indicate a separate primary failure.
- **36" gas pipeline at the Gas Terminal:** visibly intact and undamaged. The loss of containment was localised — it did not occur on the main trunk pipeline.
- **A flame-proof HPMV lamp post in the immediate vicinity** has visible damage to its enclosure: three of the bolts on the fitting are missing and the glass case is detached and standing open by approximately 5–6 cm. Whether this condition pre-existed the fire or was caused by the fire is not yet established and will be assessed by the forensic team. Until determined otherwise it is being treated as a possible ignition source candidate and has been preserved in place.
- Eight other HPMV FLP lamps in the area show varying degrees of fire damage to cables and fittings.
- Fire-water system performed during the incident: tank levels and header pressure remained in their normal bands throughout. Three of the four electrical fire-water pumps (47PE003 A, C, D) ran during cooling. (Diesel-pump availability at the time of the event was already compromised — see §10.)

---

## 6. Initial damage assessment

- **Total loss / write-off (preliminary):** condensate metering skid 310 area — meters, instrumentation, immediate piping, instrument cabling.
- **Significant damage:** electrical fittings within ~15 m radius (FLP lamps, conduit, junction boxes, the CCTV camera and its cable).
- **Fire-induced secondary damage:** to surrounding insulation, paint coatings, and minor structural members.
- **No damage:** main 36" and 42" trunk pipelines; Slug Catcher Phase-I body (isolated in time); main control rooms and Emergency Control Room.
